 @thiblahute was developed a simple but useful command line for this: \r\nhttps://gitlab.gnome.org/thiblahute/matrix-dl\r\n\r\nIn order to install matrix-dl without messing our system's Python setup, we will document how to install it using a virtual environment. The command virtualenv is provided by a Python package that enable the creation of these virtual environments. You can install virtualenv using you packaging system.\r\n\r\nRun:\r\n\r\n```\r\nvirtualenv -p python3 matrix\r\ncd matrix\r\nsource bin/activate\r\n```\r\n\r\nNow, clone the code:\r\n\r\n```\r\ngit clone https://gitlab.gnome.org/thiblahute/matrix-dl.git\r\n```\r\n\r\nAnd install the dependencies and the script itself in the virtual enviornment:\r\n\r\n```\r\ncd matrix-dl\r\npython setup.py install\r\n```\r\n\r\nUsage:\r\n\r\nThe tool's usage instructions are these:\r\n\r\n```\r\nmatrix-dl [-h] [--password PASSWORD] [--matrix-url MATRIX_URL]\r\n          [--start-date START_DATE]\r\n          username room\r\n```\r\n\r\nDownload backlogs from Matrix as raw test\r\n\r\n```\r\npositional arguments:\r\n  username\r\n  room\r\n\r\noptional arguments:\r\n  -h, --help               show this help message and exit\r\n  --password PASSWORD      Will be asked later if not provided\r\n  --matrix-url MATRIX_URL\r\n  --start-date START_DATE  format %d%m%Y\r\n```\r\n\r\nA couple examples:\r\n\r\nLet's download the conversations from Example channel since the beginning of 2018:\r\n\r\n```\r\nmatrix-dl --matrix-url https://matrix.example.com/ --start-date 01012018 \\\r\n  \u003cfsurname\u003e \"Example\" \u003e example-2018.log\r\n```\r\n\r\nThen you will be asked for you password, and if there is no errors, the conversations will be dumped in the file example-2018.log with the format hh:mm:ss — @user: message\r\n\r\nYou can also dump conversation from unnamed rooms, such as personal conversation, you just need the room's internal ID. class="markdown-body" data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">Nobody requires riot-web to store data. riot-web is just the user frontend and it pulls data from the hs all the time. If the user wants to store selected data the user frontend should provide a way to do so.</p>
<p dir="auto">Using another tool is a crutch at best. How would the average enduser even install matrix-recorder? Not to mention <a href="https://gitlab.com/argit/matrix-recorder/issues/1" rel="nofollow">https://gitlab.com/argit/matrix-recorder/issues/1</a> which makes the tool unusable for everybody who's in several high traffic rooms (which no sane person would want to archive). Also routinely archieving multi-user rooms without any reason or need to do so (just because the tool happens to be catch-all) defies every purpose of data protection. It might be allowed as long as you don't publish the data but it sounds immoral to me. I would not want to do that.</p>
<p dir="auto">And regarding encryption: Matrix has already problems handling E2EE if more than one device is involved. It regularly breaks for no obvious reasons (issues are up here on github). I would not want to recommend using another device to anybody.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"><div data-testid="markdown-body" data-team-hovercards-enabled="true" class="markdown-body" data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">JFYI,  <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/thiblahute/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/thiblahute">@thiblahute</a> was developed a simple but useful command line for this:<br>
<a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/thiblahute/matrix-dl" rel="nofollow">https://gitlab.gnome.org/thiblahute/matrix-dl</a></p>
<p dir="auto">In order to install matrix-dl without messing our system's Python setup, we will document how to install it using a virtual environment. The command virtualenv is provided by a Python package that enable the creation of these virtual environments. You can install virtualenv using you packaging system.</p>
<p dir="auto">Run:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="virtualenv -p python3 matrix
cd matrix
source bin/activate"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">virtualenv -p python3 matrix
cd matrix
source bin/activate
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Now, clone the code:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="git clone https://gitlab.gnome.org/thiblahute/matrix-dl.git"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">git clone https://gitlab.gnome.org/thiblahute/matrix-dl.git
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">And install the dependencies and the script itself in the virtual enviornment:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="cd matrix-dl
python setup.py install"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">cd matrix-dl
python setup.py install
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Usage:</p>
<p dir="auto">The tool's usage instructions are these:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="matrix-dl [-h] [--password PASSWORD] [--matrix-url MATRIX_URL]
          [--start-date START_DATE]
          username room"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">matrix-dl [-h] [--password PASSWORD] [--matrix-url MATRIX_URL]
          [--start-date START_DATE]
          username room
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Download backlogs from Matrix as raw test</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="positional arguments:
  username
  room

optional arguments:
  -h, --help               show this help message and exit
  --password PASSWORD      Will be asked later if not provided
  --matrix-url MATRIX_URL
  --start-date START_DATE  format %d%m%Y"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">positional arguments:
  username
  room

optional arguments:
  -h, --help               show this help message and exit
  --password PASSWORD      Will be asked later if not provided
  --matrix-url MATRIX_URL
  --start-date START_DATE  format %d%m%Y
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">A couple examples:</p>
<p dir="auto">Let's download the conversations from Example channel since the beginning of 2018:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="matrix-dl --matrix-url https://matrix.example.com/ --start-date 01012018 \
  <fsurname> "Example" > example-2018.log"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">matrix-dl --matrix-url https://matrix.example.com/ --start-date 01012018 \
  <fsurname> "Example" > example-2018.log
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Then you will be asked for you password, and if there is no errors, the conversations will be dumped in the file example-2018.log with the format hh:mm:ss — <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/user/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/user">@user</a>: message</p>
<p dir="auto">You can also dump conversation from unnamed rooms, such as personal conversation, you just need the room's internal ID. You can get this string in riot by clicking in the room's settings icon (the gear so far) and at the end of the settings, in the advanced section, there's the room's ID:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="matrix-dl --matrix-url https://matrix.example.com/ --start-date 01012018 \
  <fsurname> \!i4BiDaYPkvfbcWdAgb:example.com > my-chat-2018.log"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">matrix-dl --matrix-url https://matrix.example.com/ --start-date 01012018 \
  <fsurname> \!i4BiDaYPkvfbcWdAgb:example.com > my-chat-2018.log
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Remember to escape the symbol !, otherwise the shell may consider it an operator.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"><div I realised i don’t actually necessarily understand what the 63 people upvoting are after here. is it:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>👍 - ability to export logs from Riot/Web for a given room(s) as a big lump of static HTML, suitable for printing or grepping or sharing out of band? This is hard, given public rooms can easily have millions of messages, and you would probably run out of RAM (or bandwidth or time) trying to export them. But we could implement it with a date range or msgcount limit.</li>
<li>❤️ - ability for Riot/Desktop to save all the messages it sees on disk as HTML or plain text, a bit like an IRC client would, spidering to fill in any gaps in the logs?</li>
<li>🚀 - actually, pantalaimon / matrix-recorder / matrix-dl etc actually have solved this already for my use case.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Seshat may help with option 2 in the near future. Meanwhile, i may be able to tweak the clipboard code to easily support option 1.</p>

<p dir="auto">i’ve been thinking about this while implementing a smarter clipboard for riot-web. I realised i don’t actually necessarily understand what the 63 people upvoting are after here. is it:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="1. +1 - ability to export logs from Riot/Web for a given room(s) as a big lump of static HTML, suitable for printing or grepping or sharing out of band? But we could implement it with a date range or msgcount limit.

2. heart - ability for Riot/Desktop to save all the messages it sees on disk as HTML or plain text, a bit like an IRC client would, spidering to fill in any gaps in the logs?

3. rocket - actually, pantalaimon / matrix-recorder / matrix-dl etc actually have solved this already for my use case."><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">1. +1 - ability to export logs from Riot/Web for a given room(s) as a big lump of static HTML, suitable for printing or grepping or sharing out of band? But we could implement it with a date range or msgcount limit.

2. heart - ability for Riot/Desktop to save all the messages it sees on disk as HTML or plain text, a bit like an IRC client would, spidering to fill in any gaps in the logs?

3. rocket - actually, pantalaimon / matrix-recorder / matrix-dl etc actually have solved this already for my use case.

data-testid="markdown-body" data-team-hovercards-enabled="true" class="markdown-body" data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">Let me reformulate how bad the lack of offline history is, in hopes to increase its priority.</p>
<p dir="auto">Imagine we have a community using a chat system not only to share cat picz but to build something great towards a big goal. Like an open source or an open hardware project. In the process we share valuable <strong>knowledge</strong> and ideas in this chat. In other words, we rely on chat for something serious.</p>
<p dir="auto">Now consider the same scenario for two systems.</p>
<p dir="auto">A: Any decade-old IRC or XMPP client:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>enable saving of chat logs to local text files</li>
<li>chat with your community for years, accumulating knowledge</li>
<li>the single server we all used is gone (for whatever reason)</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Result: a lot of members have replicas of community's entire chat history and can cooperate to quickly respawn it in a new location.</p>
<p dir="auto">B: Matrix flagship client (Element) in 2020:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>chat with your community for years, accumulating knowledge</li>
<li>the single server we all used is gone (for whatever reason)</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Result: there is a high chance that everything is lost. If we are lucky, admins of participating homeservers will help to recover <em>some</em> of the lost content. Now we have to scratch our heads: how does s2s replication work? Do homeservers replicate the entirety of <em>all</em> rooms or only slices of rooms relevant to homeserver's users?</p>
<p dir="auto">I didn't study other Matrix clients but I assume it is the same for many.</p>
<p dir="auto">Now I open matrix.org:</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto">An open network for secure, <strong>decentralized</strong> communication</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">and</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Matrix is really a decentralised conversation store rather than a messaging protocol.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">and so on.</p>
<p dir="auto">Considering the practical difficulty of running homeservers let me ask a simple question: What is more decentralized?</p>
<p dir="auto">a. 1 central IRC server + 10 always-online users that save chat logs and publish them somewhere + 50 users who periodically sync them</p>
<p dir="auto">b. 1-3 Matrix homeservers you will find in small communities + <strong>0</strong> users saving chat logs</p>
<p dir="auto">I should also mention that in the IRC scenario it is practically impossible to delete messages from users' local files. In Matrix it is possible to delete messages and while I hope the database is append-only, I'm not sure it is possible for users to recover deleted messages in all cases.</p>
<p dir="auto">Closing my mini-rant, Matrix is the best open-source, actively-developed, semi-decentralized, self-hosted, E2EE-enabled chat system I am aware of. I highly respect what Matrix is doing and I am very thankful that we now have a decent alternative to Slack/Discord/Telegram where freedom and sovereignty mean something.</p>
<p dir="auto">The point of this message is to make a case that from a <em>user perspective</em>, as it is today, Matrix is <strong>less decentralized</strong> than IRC. I don't want to sound too negative, but such system is <em>training</em> end users to rely on servers and believe/hope everything will be fine. And all of it comes from one missing feature: easy-to-save offline history that keeps a copy of the knowledge the community generates every day.</p>
<p dir="auto">I kindly ask to reconsider the priority of offline history.</p>
<p dir="auto">Thank you for your attention.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"><div class="ReactionPopoverAnchor__B84pko"><button dir="auto">A webapp, as in a standalone Javascript app running in a supported web browser cannot write to your filesystem. It can (on explicit user interaction, e.g a download button) download a file but cannot just keep appending to a file.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/File_System_Access_API" rel="nofollow">https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/File_System_Access_API</a> / <a href="https://web.dev/file-system-access/" rel="nofollow">https://web.dev/file-system-access/</a> would allow for the latter but the user's consent would not persist between sessions plus the API is still a working draft. Forcing the user to consent each time they reload the app would not be a user-friendly experience.</p>
